# Make vessel park choreography a registered, replaceable owner

## Context

The [#18304 extensibility audit](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5560546655) named `VesselPark` as an unregistered candidate. A fresh-process probe now verifies its specific gap: install `Neo.overwrites.Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselPark.restore = () => false`, create the existing handlers, park and convert out. The factory still returns `true` and calls the re-show effect once; the Neo namespace is absent.

## The Problem

`createVesselParkHandlers` closes over one gesture's state and internal effect/restore methods. Its supplied platform callbacks are configurable, but applications cannot specialize the internal choreography through the ordinary Neo class/overwrite path. The two consumer classes already compose this shared module, so adding methods to Workspace would leave the sibling DemoB consumer behind.

## The Architectural Reality

VesselPark owns only gesture-local admission and pending-transition state. Native window ownership stays with the Group; the host supplies strict `parkVessel`, `reshowVessel`, and `disposeVessel` effects. Workstation constructs two independent handler sets and DemoB one. Existing controls cover strict synchronous/asynchronous admission, restore on cancel, commit-only disposal, duplicate terminal coalescing and external retirement.

## The Fix

Convert the existing `window/VesselPark.mjs` to a registered Base-derived `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselPark` class with effect callbacks as configs, state per instance, and internal dispatch through methods. Preserve public handler/getter names and payloads. Replace the three factory calls with Neo.create and explicitly destroy each consumer-owned instance. Remove the factory export and lexical-helper implementation; keep a single choreography owner.

Destroy invalidates pending continuations and clears this gesture owner without calling native platform effects or taking over Group-owned windows. Tests must distinguish this from an asynchronous completion resurrecting disposed state.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Refusal/default | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VesselPark owner | Base/config/overwrite path | Registered per-instance class; internal restore/effect decisions replaceable | Required platform callbacks remain required | Class/config/method JSDoc | Actual overwrite and subclass probes |
| Park/out/terminal/retirement handlers | Existing VesselPark contract | Same strict effects, exact-once ordering and identity/rect payloads | Refusal retains retry state; non-commit restores | Existing choreography docs | Existing sync/async regression controls |
| Consumer lifetime | Workstation and DemoB composition | Three independent Neo-created owners, retired with their host | Destruction fences late continuations; no platform effect from destroy | Teardown JSDoc | Owner isolation and pending-destroy tests |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One registered Base class replaces the factory; method dispatch and a real Neo.overwrites/subclass customization reach the internal restore path.
- [ ] Existing strict admission, rect fallback, cancel/commit behavior, duplicate coalescing and external-retirement controls remain green for sync and async effects.
- [ ] Independent instances do not share state. Destroying during pending park/restore/terminal work cannot publish state or invoke a later platform effect.
- [ ] Workstation and DemoB use and destroy the registered owners; no factory alias, second state machine, Group/native ownership change or copied consumer choreography.
- [ ] Focused owner/consumer tests and the full unit suite pass; generated class hierarchy and JSDoc identify the owner.

## Out of Scope

Euclid's #18398 Participation/embodiment staging, native platform park/re-show bodies, geometry or arbitration changes, the human pointer-overlap journey, other factory conversions, getRefreshOptions, Brain/tooling work, or changes to merged PRs.

## Avoided Traps

A registered wrapper over the old closure; singleton gesture state; importing dock behavior into the generic Group manager; making destruction acquire or close native windows; silently changing strict Boolean admission while changing ownership.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029; choreography and native authority unchanged.
Decision Record: existing ADR 0029 remains authoritative.
